Empirical Bayes shares on a code hierarchy

Source: R/share_intervals.R
eb_share_tree.Rd

Shrinks the shares of the codes of a hierarchy towards a prior mean with a concentration estimated from the data, and returns posterior means and credible intervals.

Usage

eb_share_tree(
  est,
  key_col,
  parent_col,
  level_col,
  type = c("partition", "overlap"),
  prior_mean = NULL,
  deff_col = NULL,
  conf = 0.95,
  draws = 2000L,
  x_col = "x",
  n_col = "n",
  tol = 1e-08
)

Arguments

est

data.frame or data.table with one row per node and columns key_col, parent_col, level_col, x_col, n_col.

key_col

Name of the node identifier column.

parent_col

Name of the parent column (NA or "" for roots).

level_col

Name of the level column; parents must have a lower level than their children.

type

"partition" (children partition the parent, e.g. professions with an "unknown" category) or "overlap" (each node has its own count with no sum constraint, e.g. postings with at least one skill of a group).

prior_mean

Optional name of a column with the prior mean. For "partition" it is the conditional share child | parent (renormalised within each family); for "overlap" it is the share of the node. See Details for the default.

deff_col

Optional name of a design effect column; counts are divided by it before the fit.

conf

Credibility level, default 0.95.

draws

Number of posterior draws for "partition" (default 2000). Set the seed with set.seed() before the call for reproducible intervals; the function does not set it.

x_col, n_col

Names of the count and denominator columns (defaults "x", "n").

tol

Tolerance of the coherence checks (default 1e-8).

Value

A copy of est with columns quota_eb (posterior mean), lo_eb, hi_eb (credible interval), kappa_famiglia (estimated concentration of the family the node belongs to; NA when not estimable, Inf when the data show no extra dispersion around the prior mean) and vincoli_ok (coherence check on parent nodes, NA on leaves).

Details

Partition. A family is the set of children of one parent (the roots form one family with total n). Within a family the children counts x_c must sum to the parent count (to n for the roots). Counts are divided by the family design effect, the x-weighted mean of the children deff. The family vector follows a Dirichlet-multinomial with mean m (the prior mean, or the uniform share 1 / K when prior_mean is NULL) and concentration kappa, estimated by maximising the Dirichlet-multinomial likelihood of the family. The joint likelihood is used instead of separate beta-binomial margins because it is the exact law of the family vector: the margins share the same kappa and are dependent, so their product would count the same information more than once. The posterior of the conditional shares is Dirichlet(kappa m + x_eff); families are independent, so the posterior mean of a marginal share is the product of the conditional posterior means along the path to the root, and the posterior means of the children sum to that of the parent exactly. Intervals are quantiles of draws posterior draws (normalised Gamma variables) multiplied along the path.

Overlap. For each family kappa is estimated from the beta-binomial likelihood of the children with their own prior means (see fit_betabinom()); the posterior of each node is Beta(kappa m + x_eff, kappa (1 - m) + n_eff - x_eff) and the interval uses its quantiles. Without prior_mean no shrinkage of the mean is applied: quota_eb = x / n and the interval is the Jeffreys interval on the effective counts; the hierarchy then acts only through the design effect. vincoli_ok checks, on parent nodes, max(children) <= parent <= min(1, sum(children)) up to tol.

A concentration at the upper bound (1e8) is reported as Inf and the posterior collapses on the prior mean; the uncertainty about kappa is not propagated (empirical Bayes).

References

Mosimann, J. E. (1962). On the compound multinomial distribution, the multivariate beta-distribution, and correlations among proportions. Biometrika, 49(1/2), 65-82.

Efron, B. and Morris, C. (1975). Data analysis using Stein's estimator and its generalizations. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 70(350), 311-319.

Examples

est <- data.frame(
  code = c("A", "B", "A1", "A2", "B1", "B2"),
  parent = c(NA, NA, "A", "A", "B", "B"),
  level = c(1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 2),
  x = c(600, 400, 590, 10, 200, 200),
  n = 1000
)
set.seed(1)
eb_share_tree(est, "code", "parent", "level", draws = 500)
#>      code parent level     x     n   quota_eb       lo_eb      hi_eb
#>    <char> <char> <num> <num> <num>      <num>       <num>      <num>
#> 1:      A   <NA>     1   600  1000 0.59750376 0.565621973 0.62639415
#> 2:      B   <NA>     1   400  1000 0.40249624 0.373605848 0.43437803
#> 3:     A1      A     2   590  1000 0.58727570 0.555143383 0.61531074
#> 4:     A2      A     2    10  1000 0.01022806 0.005398466 0.01713123
#> 5:     B1      B     2   200  1000 0.20124812 0.186813982 0.21720580
#> 6:     B2      B     2   200  1000 0.20124812 0.186791866 0.21717547
#>    kappa_famiglia vincoli_ok
#>             <num>     <lgcl>
#> 1:     25.6014867       TRUE
#> 2:     25.6014867       TRUE
#> 3:      0.5607706         NA
#> 4:      0.5607706         NA
#> 5:            Inf         NA
#> 6:            Inf         NA
